title: IB Theatre Coursework Timeline: September-November
summary: Plan your IB Theatre coursework timeline from September to November, with realistic milestones for research, practical work, evidence, reflection, and review.
body_markdown:
### IB Theatre Coursework Timeline: September-November


The best **IB Theatre coursework timeline** starts in September, not when the first formal deadline appears. Use September to understand the task and establish an evidence system, October to investigate and experiment, and November to turn your work into a structured artistic argument or process account.


Exact requirements depend on your course version, level, examination session, and school calendar. Your teacher sets internal checkpoints, while official IB materials define the assessment requirements. This timeline is therefore a practical fall schedule, not a replacement for your current Theatre guide.


### Confirm which IB Theatre course applies to you


IB Theatre changed with the course first taught in **2022** and first assessed in **2024** . In the current course, the **Production Proposal** is internally assessed at SL and HL, while the **Collaborative Project** is internally assessed at HL. The Research Presentation and Solo Theatre Piece are externally assessed, although students complete much of their preparation at school.


Older online advice may refer to the Director's Notebook or describe the Collaborative Project as SL internal assessment. These details belong to the previous course and should not be transferred automatically. Before planning, confirm:


- your examination session and course version;
- whether you take SL or HL;
- the exact assessed component;
- school deadlines for drafts, rehearsals, recordings, and submission;
- current evidence, citation, page, and time requirements.


The official[IB Theatre subject page](https://www.ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/the-arts/theatre/) and[Theatre subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/theatre-sl-hl-2024-en.pdf) provide an overview. Use the full guide supplied through your school for detailed criteria and instructions.


### What should start in September?


Start the process immediately, but do not write a polished submission before investigating and experimenting. Convincing Theatre coursework shows that decisions developed through research, practical trials, feedback, and revision.


Create one reliable evidence system during the first week. A digital folder, process journal, or combination can work if it contains:


- source notes and complete bibliographic details;
- dated rehearsal or workshop entries;
- permitted photographs, sketches, plans, and diagrams;
- feedback and records of resulting changes;
- explanations of intentions, experiments, decisions, and evaluation;
- filenames identifying the date, activity, and version.


Collecting evidence does not mean submitting everything. It allows you to select the strongest permitted examples later.


### September-to-November IB Theatre coursework timeline


Period Main priority Concrete outcome


September, weeks 1-2 Decode the task Annotated criteria, deadlines, evidence folders, and an initial focus


September, weeks 3-4 Investigate possibilities Research notes, stimulus or text analysis, questions, and early practical tests


October, weeks 1-2 Experiment systematically Documented performance, direction, design, or collaborative alternatives


October, weeks 3-4 Develop and select A justified artistic direction and organised practical evidence


November, weeks 1-2 Build the assessed explanation A detailed outline, selected evidence, and substantial first draft


November, weeks 3-4 Review and improve Criterion-based revisions, technical checks, and a December plan


### September: understand, organise, and test ideas


Translate each criterion into plain language. Ask what you must **demonstrate** , which evidence could make that visible, and what weaker responses often omit. Put school deadlines on a calendar and work backwards, separating practical development, documentation, drafting, feedback, and final assembly.


During weeks 3-4, alternate between research and studio exploration. For a Production Proposal, investigate the prescribed material, context, intended audience experience, staging, and relevant production elements. For an HL Collaborative Project, establish working agreements, explore starting points through workshops, and record how different contributions affect the emerging work.


By the end of September, aim for a workable direction rather than a fixed concept. You should have focused questions, credible sources, early experiments, and reasons for developing some possibilities instead of others.


### October: test theatrical choices


October should contain sustained practical experimentation. Give each session a precise question, such as how proximity changes the audience's relationship with a performer or how lighting supports a particular atmosphere.


Document alternatives, not only the final choice. Record the intention, what you tried, what observers or collaborators noticed, and what you changed next. This provides specific evidence of artistic development instead of a general rehearsal diary.


For collaborative work, assign practical responsibilities while preserving genuinely shared artistic development. Record disagreements and revisions when they affected the theatre piece, but focus on their artistic significance rather than listing meetings.


By the end of October, you should be able to explain your intentions using research and practical evidence. If the concept remains vague, narrow the intended audience effect, performance space, key moment, or production element.


### November: draft and diagnose gaps


Begin a substantial outline or draft before mid-November. Organise it around the required structure and assessment criteria, not simply the order in which events occurred. Pair each claim with specific evidence and explain why the decision matters theatrically.


A useful analytical sequence is:


1. State the artistic intention or problem.
2. Describe the relevant research, experiment, or collaborative action.
3. Explain what changed and why.
4. Connect the choice to performance, production, space, or audience experience.
5. Evaluate limitations or identify the next step where appropriate.


During the final two weeks, check that visuals are relevant and legible, citations are complete, required sections are present, evidence is permitted, and the work follows current formal limits. Finish November with specific December tasks rather than an instruction to simply finish the coursework.


### Adapting the timeline to each internal component


Component Level September October November


Production Proposal SL and HL Analyse prescribed material and establish preliminary intentions Test staging and production possibilities Develop the proposal, integrate purposeful visuals, and revise against criteria


Collaborative Project HL Establish ensemble processes and explore starting points Devise, rehearse, receive feedback, and refine Consolidate performance material and organise the process account


HL students should protect Collaborative Project rehearsal dates first. Group availability, performance spaces, and rehearsal continuity are harder to replace than individual writing time.


### A weekly routine that prevents backlog


Reserve three recurring blocks during September-November:


- **Practical block, 60-90 minutes:** rehearse, stage, design, facilitate, or test one question.
- **Documentation block, 20-30 minutes:** label evidence and record what changed.
- **Development block, 45-60 minutes:** research, analyse, storyboard, draft, or revise one criterion.


Complete documentation within 24 hours of a rehearsal. Instead of writing that a session went well, identify the exact choice, its observed effect, the feedback received, and the resulting revision.


RevisionDojo's[IB Theatre resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-theatre) can help you review concepts, while[Jojo AI](https://www.revisiondojo.com/jojo-ai) can question your reasoning or identify vague explanations. AI should support reflection, not replace your theatrical process, evidence, or authorship.


### Common timeline mistakes


- **Waiting for a final concept:** Document uncertainty, rejected options, and changes because they demonstrate development.
- **Researching without practical application:** Turn each useful source into a theatrical question and test it.
- **Collecting unexplained photographs:** Explain what each image shows and how it supports analysis.
- **Treating feedback as editing:** Ask targeted questions, then retain responsibility for every decision.
- **Using an outdated checklist:** Match all requirements to your session, level, component, and current guide.


By 30 November, you should have sustained research, several documented experiments, an emerging artistic intention, organised evidence, a substantial outline or draft, and a precise list of remaining work. Prioritise missing practical evidence and criterion coverage before polishing language.


### Conclusion


A strong **IB Theatre coursework timeline** uses September for understanding and exploration, October for testing alternatives, and November for structured analysis and review. Keep your plan aligned with the current guide and your teacher's deadlines.
